divergence_notes.note: metrics.solver_use and metrics.authority_receipt.ranking_eligible are unconditional runtime admission requirements but only conditional schema requirements. A schema-only consumer will hand the optimizer envelopes the optimizer cannot read. Phase-1 repair: hoist both keys into metrics.required unconditionally.

The zero-authority quarantine lives ONLY in Rust. A downstream consumer validating against the published schema alone would accept usable_by_optimizer=true, a non-empty objective vector, a released ranking lock, missing claim locks and solver_use=OBJECTIVE. Today the runtime holds the line; the published contract does not state it.
Conversely the schema rejects presentation/range/enum/pattern violations the admission path admits. Neither decider subsumes the other -- they are incomparable.

metrics.allOf[0] is keyed on metrics.model_receipt_schema, which the EMITTER controls. Every clause is load-bearing when the trigger is set (14/14 ablations rejected) and every clause is void when it is not. Phase-1 repair options: (i) trigger the gate on the presence of metrics.primary_prediction instead, (ii) make model_receipt_schema itself unconditionally required for status=SCORED, or (iii) require prediction_status=NOT_RUN whenever the trigger is absent.

does_not_close: Reason-level parity: only ADMIT/REJECT verdicts are claimed; the runtime error taxonomy is not compared against schema error paths.
Whether to repair by tightening the schema or by relaxing the runtime is a Phase-1 design decision, not an audit call.
Cross-module conformance of the 29 consumers' actually-emitted score envelopes at run time (only the module's own shipped fixtures were available on disk).
Coverage-guided fuzzing of the admission path; hard-constraint and objective evaluation paths (the corpus uses an empty KPI profile by construction).
No promotion, no manifest edit, no scientific_readiness flip, no wet-lab, qualification, or release authority.

G1_core_parity.note: On the shared-requirement core (8 jointly-dereferenced required keys, 3 escalated authority tiers, 6 conformant positives) the declarative schema and the compiled runtime must agree case-for-case. ANY disagreement here REFUTES core admission parity.

G2_runtime_superset_provenance.note: The runtime unconditionally requires metrics.solver_use and metrics.authority_receipt.ranking_eligible; the schema requires them only under the opt-in model_receipt_schema trigger. Schema ACCEPTS, runtime REJECTS.

G3_runtime_superset_escalation.note: The entire zero-authority quarantine (optimizer lock, empty objective vector, ranking lock, 10 required claim locks, solver ceiling) is enforced ONLY by the runtime; the published schema admits every escalation.

G4_schema_superset.note: Conversely the schema rejects 10 schema-only required keys and 9 value-level constraints (range, enum, minLength, hash pattern, model_card shape) that the runtime admission path never reads.

G5_conditional_gate_clause_necessity.note: With the trigger present, each of the 14 provenance obligations is individually load-bearing: deleting any one is rejected, and the fully populated envelope is accepted. No redundant clause.

G6_gate_fail_open_confirmed.note: REFUTATION GATE: deleting the single emitter-controlled trigger key discharges all 14 obligations, and a bare numeric primary_prediction with zero provenance binding is schema-valid. The provenance gate is opt-in, not a mandatory mediator.

G7_empirical_shipped_fixtures.note: All 6 score fixtures shipped by the module are schema-VALID and runtime-INADMISSIBLE, and remain inadmissible after module_id is repaired to a registered module -- so the refusal is the missing provenance/quarantine fields, not registration.

G8_runtime_oracle_determinism.note: Every runtime verdict reproduced by a second independent rank_candidates construction inside the same process.

headline: H0 REFUTED, BIDIRECTIONALLY: the published score-envelope schema is NOT the binding optimizer-admission contract. Core parity holds exactly (17/17), but the runtime is a strict reject-superset on the provenance (32 cases total: 4 provenance + 16 zero-authority-quarantine) while the schema is a strict reject-superset on 30 presentation/range/enum cases. The schema's 15-clause provenance gate is clause-necessary (14/14) but FAIL-OPEN: it is keyed on an emitter-controlled trigger, so a numeric prediction with zero provenance binding is schema-valid -- and all 6/6 shipped score fixtures are schema-valid yet 6/6 runtime-inadmissible.

hypothesis.interpretation: The two deciders are INCOMPARABLE, not equivalent. (a) RUNTIME-STRICTER: the optimizer front door unconditionally dereferences /metrics/solver_use and /metrics/authority_receipt/ranking_eligible and enforces the whole zero-authority quarantine (usable_by_optimizer=false, empty objective_values, ranking lock down, all 10 REQUIRED_ZERO_AUTHORITY_CLAIM_LOCKS true, solver_use within {DISABLED, AUDIT_ONLY, CONSTRAINT_ONLY}, module registered); the schema constrains none of that -- claim_locks and objective_values are free objects, usable_by_optimizer is a free boolean, and OBJECTIVE/R&D_OBJECTIVE are INSIDE the schema's solver_use enum but ABOVE the runtime ceiling. (b) SCHEMA-STRICTER: 10 schema-required keys plus score_0_1 range, status/score_semantics enums, evidence_scope minLength, model_card shape and the 64-hex hash pattern are never read by the admission path. (c) FAIL-OPEN GATE: metrics.allOf[0] fires only on metrics.model_receipt_schema, a key the emitting module chooses to write; every one of its 14 obligations is individually load-bearing when it fires, and every one of them evaporates when it does not. This inverts Saltzer & Schroeder's fail-safe-defaults and complete-mediation principles: the default is permit, and the mediator is bypassable by omission. The empirical layer confirms this is not hypothetical -- 0/6 of the module's own shipped score fixtures set the trigger, 2 of them carry score_0_1=1.0 with usable_by_optimizer=true, and all 6 are schema-valid.
hypothesis.statement: the published score-envelope JSON Schema and the compiled optimizer admission path accept and reject the same typed corpus of score envelopes

non_circularity: Two independently-authored deciders. Oracle A is the on-disk declarative score-envelope JSON Schema enforced by jsonschema 4.26.0 over CPython json. Oracle B is the compiled Rust amphora-core optimizer admission path reached through the public rank_candidates entry point (which internally runs the private optimizer_envelopes extraction and authorize_optimizer_request). Neither oracle was fitted to the other; the per-case LAYER and BOTH per-case verdict PREDICTIONS were declared in a third artifact (build_score_corpus.py) from the module semantics before either oracle ran. The empirical layer uses the module's own shipped fixtures verbatim, which predate this study.

oracle_B_runtime.entry_point: public rank_candidates(&[Value], &KpiProfile) with an empty profile; verdict = RankedCandidate.feasible
oracle_B_runtime.policy: quarantined_optimizer_policy() -- ranking disabled, solver disabled, authority expansion forbidden, decision ceiling AUDIT_ONLY

purpose: Audit the SCORE half of the candidate contract -- the output envelope that 29 consumer modules and the optimizer front door depend on -- by differentially testing the on-disk declarative schema against the compiled optimizer admission path, and by ablating every clause of the schema's conditional provenance gate for necessity and for fail-safe behaviour.
